thread:
sarah: quick report — after the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration I'm seeing a cluster of broken deep-links (hash fragments) from our /guides/* pages. some redirect to the top of the page, others 404.

matt: ah ok. can you paste an example URL?

sarah: yes — e.g. https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/streaming#response-buffering (returns 404) while https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/streaming#response-buffer works. looks like slug normalization changed for headings with parentheses / slashes.

ana: fwiw docusaurus slugify rules differ from mkdocs. parens and slashes often get dropped or replaced.

matt: repro steps?

sarah: quick check I did:
```bash
# find files referencing the old hashes
grep -R "#response-buffering" docs || true
# list headings in the target doc to see generated slugs
grep -n "^#" docs/guides/streaming.md || true
```

ravi: deploy-bot link-checker flagged 27 failing fragment links in last run. looks concentrated in /guides and /examples.

docbot: link-checker report -> https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/7890/linkcheck (summary: 27 fails, 12 redirects, 3 404s)

matt: thanks. plan suggestion: 1) add explicit frontmatter aliases/permalinks where possible 2) batch-fix references for obvious slug diffs 3) add a small note in the migration guide about slug differences so external links don't silently break.

ana: for docusaurus we can add `slug` or `aliases` in the frontmatter of the MDX to preserve old hashes. example: 
```yaml
---
slug: /guides/streaming
aliases: ["/guides/streaming#response-buffering"]
---
```
this will make old links work without changing headings.

ravi: are we ok with adding aliases en masse? need to check performance/size of redirects list in the build.

matt: aliases are fine for a handful; for >100 we should instead run a bulk replace across docs to normalize links. also prefer canonical slugs in content.

ana: I'll prepare a small script to generate alias blocks for the highest-traffic pages (guides/examples/SDK snippets). it will create PRs with frontmatter edits only.

sarah: thanks. I'll assemble a list of failing URLs (from link-checker) and mark which ones are external vs internal.

ravi: for cases where external partners link to deep-section anchors we might also add netlify/_redirects rules as a fallback (temporary).

matt: good idea — fallback redirect only while aliases propagate. open a tiny RFC / PR for redirects with TTL and we can remove later.

ana: quick draft of the alias-generator I plan to run: 
```python
# alias-generator.py (very small)
# reads link-checker CSV, maps failing fragment -> file, inserts alias in frontmatter if not present
# usage: python alias-generator.py failing-fragments.csv --dry-run
```
I'll push WIP to #5427.

sarah: note for SDK snippets: some of our snippet files use headings like `Getting started (Python)` which produced slugs like `getting-started-python` in mkdocs but `getting-started-python-1` in docusaurus because of duplicate heading ids. we'll need to check duplicates too.

matt: good catch. duplicates produce `-1` suffixes, which breaks exact old hashes. prefer to dedupe headings or add explicit ids in MDX where needed.

ravi: I'll check link-checker to produce a prioritized list (freq of external hits + internal references). target small batch (top 20) for aliases first.

deploy-bot: CI link-check step failed on branch fix/doc-fragments-2026 — see https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/7901 (logs) :x:

ana: ack, will re-run after I push a clean PR. planning to open PRs scoped to: guides (5 files), examples (7 files), sdk-snippets (3 files).

sarah: for the migration guide, can we add a short section: "fragment/slug changes" with examples and a short recommendation (aliases > bulk content edits)? I can draft it.

matt: yes please. make it a short table + examples. add the alias YAML example and one `id`/heading fix example.

ana: PRs: #5427 (alias generator WIP), #5431 (guides frontmatter fixes), #5432 (examples fixes). I'll add checklists for reviewers.

ravi: I'll coordinate with infra about adding temporary redirect rules after we push the first PRs.

matt: timeline: aim for staggered PRs this week, run link-check CI after each. if link-check still flags >5 new failures we revert and iterate.

sarah: thanks everyone — I'll circle back with the failing-URL list in ~2h. :thumbsup:

ana: thanks — ping me if you want me to triage specific files. :sparkles:
